harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every command (with user and timestamp) to /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a sudoers.d drop-in, disabling sudo's syslog output so entries no longer land in journald/rsyslog's general system log (/var/log/secure). Verified before and after a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (RHEL 10.0), sudo/rsyslog versions, and existing sudoers.d contents
Captured baseline: sudo logs via syslog(authpriv) into journal and /var/log/secure by default (sudo -V shows --with-logging=syslog --with-logfac=authpriv)
Wrote /etc/sudoers.d/00-sudo-logging with 'Defaults !syslog', 'Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"', 'Defaults log_year', validated with visudo -cf
Installed the drop-in with mode 0440 root:root; created /var/log/sudo-commands.log with mode 0600 root:root
Ran visudo -c to confirm full sudoers tree parses
Executed test sudo commands and confirmed entries (with user + timestamp) appear only in /var/log/sudo-commands.log, and journalctl/ /var/log/secure show no new COMMAND= lines
Captured pre-reboot baseline: boot_id, boot time, service state, file states
Triggered systemctl reboot via backgrounded/detached shell so the exec call returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed connection timed out/reset during reboot then succeeded
Confirmed boot_id and boot time changed, proving an actual reboot occurred

Post-reboot: revalidated sudoers config (visudo -c), confirmed rsyslog active, confirmed prior log entries persisted, ran a new sudo command and confirmed it was appended to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user+timestamp while absent from journal

evidence.requirement: Baseline: sudo currently logs via syslog into journal and /var/log/secure (general system log)
evidence.summary: OS/sudo version identified; sudo -V shows compiled default is syslog logging (authpriv); baseline sudo test command appears in both journalctl and /var/log/secure as COMMAND= lines

evidence.requirement: sudoers drop-in created and syntactically valid, redirecting sudo logging to dedicated file and disabling syslog
evidence.summary: /etc/sudoers.d/00-sudo-logging created with 'Defaults !syslog' and 'Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"', validated via visudo -cf and full visudo -c; file installed with correct permissions alongside 0600 log file

evidence.requirement: Every sudo command is recorded with user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log, and excluded from the general system log
evidence.summary: Test sudo commands (whoami, id) appear in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with full timestamp+user ('Sep 4 23:23:25 2026 : root : ... COMMAND=/bin/whoami'); journalctl since-mark and /var/log/secure show no new COMMAND= entries (COMMAND= count in /var/log/secure unchanged at 4, only pre-existing pam session lines present)

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: pre-reboot healthy baseline (boot identity, service health, config/data state)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 6ab6a71b-188c-48ae-971b-a6bb378b1d72, boot time 2026-08-26 10:44, rsyslog active, sudoers drop-in and log file present with 2 existing entries

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect, then node became unreachable during reboot
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately; subsequent polls show connection timed out/reset, proving the node actually went down for reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: changed boot identity proves an actual reboot occurred
evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id is 84e26190-18d5-4e62-9720-f1e9614d0b76 (different from baseline) and boot time updated to 2026-09-04 23:23

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: post-reboot recovery of sudo logging config, data persistence, and continued exclusion from general system log
evidence.summary: After reboot: visudo -c parses OK, sudoers drop-in and log file intact with correct perms, prior 2 log entries preserved, rsyslog active; new post-reboot sudo command appended to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user+timestamp while journalctl grep for sudo COMMAND= lines returned no matches (exit 1)

attempts.summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every command (with user and timestamp) to /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a sudoers.d drop-in, disabling sudo's syslog output so entries no longer land in journald/rsyslog's general system log (/var/log/secure). Verified before and after a full node reboot.
